label: rmk: subrepresentations
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk: subrepresentations}
Although the space~$\mathscr{F}{\!\!\textnormal{\footnotesize\itshape ock}}$ is not an irreducible representation of $\textnormal{\textbf{SF}} \oplus \overline{\textnormal{\textbf{SF}}}$, it is cyclically generated by the action of the generators of $\textnormal{\textbf{SF}} \oplus \overline{\textnormal{\textbf{SF}}}$ on the vector~$\boldsymbol{\omega}$.
From the explicit basis~\eqref{eq: fock basis} and the anticommutation  relations ---Lie superbrackets--- of the generators,
one can argue that the only proper subrepresentations of $\mathscr{F}{\!\!\textnormal{\footnotesize\itshape ock}}$ are the ones cyclically generated by the other ground states ---$\boldsymbol{\mathbbm{1}}$, $\boldsymbol{\xi}$, and $\boldsymbol{\theta}$---.
\hfill$\diamond$

label: prop: current modes

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The operators are well-defined if they do not depend on the choice of corner contour~$\gamma$ and the choice of field-polynomial representative~$P$.
A straightforward application of the discrete Stokes' formula ---see Section~\ref{subsubsec: discrete integration}--- combined with the discrete holomorphicity of the discrete monomials ---Proposition~\ref{prop: monomials}--- and the null fields in Example~\ref{ex: Laplacian is null} is enough to see that the operators are well-defined.
To see that the operator does not depend on the representative $P$, one just needs to remember that the product of two field polynomials with supports that are at a large enough distance is null if one of the two field polynomials is null.
For a more detailed proof see Lemmata~4.2 and 4.3 in \cite{AdameCarrillo-discrete_symplectic_fermions}.

title: Lemma
body_md:
For any local field~$P+\textnormal{\small Null}$, there exists $N\in{\mathbb Z}_{>0}$ such that for all $n\geq N$ we have
\begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{\chi}_{n} \big(\, P + \textnormal{\small Null} \,\big)
    \, = \,
    \boldsymbol{\eta}_{n} \big(\, P + \textnormal{\small Null} \,\big)
    \, = \,
     
    \mathrlap{\hspace{0pt}\overline{\scalebox{1}[1]{\phantom{\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\chi}}}}}}\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\chi}}
_{n} \big(\, P + \textnormal{\small Null} \,\big)
    \, = \,
     
    \mathrlap{\hspace{0pt}\overline{\scalebox{1}[1]{\phantom{\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\eta}}}}}}\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\eta}}
_{n} \big(\, P + \textnormal{\small Null} \,\big)
    \, = \,
    0\,.
\end{align*}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a corner contour~$\gamma$ for the action ---\eqref{eq: chi mode}--\eqref{eq: eta bar mode}--- of any current mode on $P+\textnormal{\small Null}$.
Since the discrete neighbourhood of the origin where the discrete monomials $\mathbf{u}\mapsto\mathbf{u}^{[k]}$ vanishes grows with $k$, we just need to pick $N$ big enough such that $\mathbf{u}^{[N]}$ vanishes (in the interior of and) around the contour~$\gamma$.
Then, by formulae~\eqref{eq: chi mode}--\eqref{eq: eta bar mode}, it is clear that the action of $\boldsymbol{\chi}_{n}$, $\boldsymbol{\eta}_{n}$, $ 
    \mathrlap{\hspace{0pt}\overline{\scalebox{1}[1]{\phantom{\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\chi}}}}}}\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\chi}}
_{n}$, and $ 
    \mathrlap{\hspace{0pt}\overline{\scalebox{1}[1]{\phantom{\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\eta}}}}}}\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\eta}}
_{n}$ on $P+\textnormal{\small Null}$ vanishes for $n\geq N$.

label: rmk: arbitrary scale
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk: arbitrary scale}
In each discrete approximation $\Omega^{\delta}$ of the continuum domain~$\Omega$, the linear scale of the system is proportional to $\delta$; the proportionality constant $\lambda$ is arbitrary.
There is no good reason to pick as a linear scale the edge length $\delta$ instead of the diagonal length of the square-grid plaquettes $\sqrt{2}\,\delta$ or half the length of an edge $\delta/2$.
\hfill$\diamond$
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
This arbitrariness is \emph{not} relevant in non-logarithmic theories---a change in the linear scale can be absorbed as a multiplicative factor in the local observables.
This is also the case for local fields in our theory with well-defined scaling dimensions.
However, our theory contains more exotic fields that feature logarithmic divergencies in the scaling limit.
These are the generalised eigenvectors of ${\mathbf{L}}_{0}+ 
    \mathrlap{\hspace{-1pt}\overline{\scalebox{0.85}[1]{\phantom{\ensuremath{\mathbf{L}}}}}}\ensuremath{\mathbf{L}}
_{0}$ that are not eigenvectors.
\hfill$\diamond$

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma: corrfun h-one and diss}
Let $\mathbf{z}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{z}_n,\mathbf{w}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{w}_m\in\Omega^{\delta}$ be interior vertices of $\Omega^{\delta}$.
We have
\begin{align*}
    {\mathbb E}^{\textnormal{ASM}}_{\Omega^{\delta}}
    \big[\,
    \mathsf{h}_1(\mathbf{z}_1) \cdots \mathsf{h}_1(\mathbf{z}_n)
    \,\rotatebox[]{90}{\scalebox{.65}{\textbf{ ~- - - }}}\,
    \mathsf{d}(\mathbf{w}_1) \cdots \mathsf{d}(\mathbf{w}_m)
    \,\big]
    \,=\,
    \Big\langle 
    H_1(\mathbf{z}_1) \cdots H_1(\mathbf{z}_n)
    D(\mathbf{w}_1) \cdots D(\mathbf{w}_m)
     \Big\rangle_{\Omega^{\delta}}^{\textnormal{fDGFF}}
\end{align*}
with $D(\mathbf{z}) \coloneqq \dfrac{1}{4\pi}\xi(\mathbf{z})\theta(\mathbf{z})$\,.

label: lemma: technical
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove the case $\ell = 0$ for general $k > 0$.
Recall that we defined $X_0=\boldsymbol\upxi(0)$ in Example~\ref{ex: fermion linear rep}.
We have
\begin{align*}
    \sqint_\gamma
    \mathbf{u}_\diamond^{[-k]} \,
    \wick{ \partial^\bullet_\sharp \c\boldsymbol\uptheta (\mathbf{u}_\textnormal{m}) \c{X}_{-\ell} }
    \, \textnormal{d}^{\sharp} \mathbf{u}
    \, = \,
    -4\pi
    \sqint_\gamma
    \mathbf{u}_\diamond^{[-k]} \,
    \partial^\bullet_\sharp\mathbf{G}_{{\mathbb Z}^2}(\mathbf{u}_\textnormal{m})
    \, \textnormal{d}^{\sharp} \mathbf{u}\,.
\end{align*}
Note that, away from the origin, both integrands are discrete holomorphic, so the above integral does not depend on the (large enough) discrete contour $\gamma$.
Recall that, as $\vert \mathbf{u} \vert \to \infty$, we have $\mathbf{u}^{[-k]}=\mathcal{O}\big(\vert\mathbf{u}\vert^{-k}\big)$ and $\partial^\bullet_\sharp\mathbf{G}_{{\mathbb Z}^2}(\mathbf{u})=\mathcal{O}\big(\vert\mathbf{u}\vert^{-1}\big)$.
Let $\gamma(R)$ be a discrete contour with a square shape of sidelength $R$.
The above integral has the asymptotic behaviour $\mathcal{O}\big(R^{-k}\big)$ as $ R \to \infty$, but, since it does not depend on $R$, taking the limit $R\to\infty$ we see that it  must vanish.
The case $\ell > 0$ can be handled by similar arguments---we refer the reader to \cite[Lemma~6.5]{ABK-DGFF_local_fields} for the details of these arguments in the bosonic setting.

label: lemma: converg diagonal greens fnctn
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The function,
\begin{align*}
    H^\delta
    \,\colon\,
    \mathbf{w}
    \longmapsto
    \mathbf{G}_{\Omega^{\delta}}\big(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{z}^\delta \big)
    -
    \mathbf{G}_{{\mathbb Z}^2}\bigg( \frac{\mathbf{w}-\mathbf{z}^\delta}{\delta} \bigg)
    +
    \frac{1}{2\pi}\log \delta
    -
    \frac{\mathsf{C}}{2\pi}
\end{align*}
is discrete harmonic on $\Omega^{\delta}$ and has boundary values $\frac{1}{2\pi}\log \vert \mathbf{x}^\delta - \mathbf{z}^\delta \vert + \mathcal{O}(\delta^2)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$ for $\mathbf{x}^\delta$ at the boundary of $\Omega^{\delta}$.
It is well-known that (any reasonable extension to $\Omega$ of) $H^\delta$ converges to the harmonic extension of the function $x\mapsto\frac{1}{2\pi}\log \vert x - z\vert$ on $\partial\Omega$ to the interior $\Omega$.
This limiting function on $\Omega$ is the harmonic part of the Green's function $\mathbf{g}_\Omega( \,\cdot\, ,z)$.
Evaluating $H^\delta$ at $\mathbf{z}^\delta$, we get the desired scaling limit convergence since we have $\mathbf{G}_{{\mathbb Z}^2}(0)=0$.
